details: The Trump administration announced new tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on imports from over 80 countries, including the UK, Mexico, Canada, Australia, India, China, and the EU. These measures replace earlier blanket tariffs and are justified by claims of inadequate enforcement against goods produced by forced labor. The announcement led to a sharp decline in Asian stock markets and created significant uncertainty in global trade. China has warned that trade wars are not in the interest of any party.
title: US Imposes New Tariffs on Over 80 Countries, Shaking Global Trade

details: Military tensions in the Middle East have intensified, with the US-Iran conflict escalating and Houthi rebels attacking two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea. These developments pushed Brent crude oil prices above $100 per barrel, triggering inflation fears and increasing investor risk aversion across global financial markets. US President Donald Trump has threatened a "massive attack" on Iran.
title: Middle East Tensions Escalate, Driving Oil Prices Above $100

details: The European Union adopted its 21st sanctions package against Russia, which includes targeting over 100 banks and crypto operators involved in sustaining Russia's war economy. The package introduces transaction bans on 14 crypto platforms across six jurisdictions and a new legal mechanism that could lead to full third-country bans on crypto-asset services used to evade EU sanctions.
title: EU Sanctions Package Targets Russian Crypto Platforms

details: The US CLARITY Act, aimed at providing a clear regulatory framework for digital assets, is facing a legislative deadlock. A new draft of the bill has ignited disputes between Republicans and Democrats regarding oversight power. This ongoing uncertainty is seen by analysts as a reason for major banks lowering price targets for cryptocurrencies and prolongs a period of regulatory ambiguity for crypto investors.
title: US CLARITY Act on Crypto Regulation Faces Legislative Stalemate

details: Bitcoin entered a cautious trading phase on July 24, consolidating near the $65,000 mark after declining about 0.95% in the previous 24 hours. The cryptocurrency's price action is being influenced by global developments, including Middle East tensions, rising crude oil prices, and expectations around Federal Reserve policy, as well as the uncertainty surrounding the US CLARITY Act. Rising US Treasury yields, reaching Trump-era highs, also added pressure on risk assets. Spot Bitcoin ETFs also recorded net outflows, breaking a recent positive streak.
title: Bitcoin Price Reacts to Geopolitical and Macroeconomic Headwinds
